scope: repair diff (ff9150b~1..HEAD) plus the standing round-1 findings; not a full-diff re-sweep
round1_verification: Reviewer independently re-derived each round-1 repair. R1, R2, R3 and R7 each redden the single new case when reverted at their real call sites, confirming the combined-catch claim. R7's numeric claim reproduces exactly: recomputing every row of both committed soak reports under answers_match + status=='success' gives 8/10 and 7/10 unchanged, and all 25 committed soak rows are measured:true, so D20's 10/10 survives the R1 rule change. R6 is genuinely derived (adding a throwaway case file turned docs-numbers-are-derived red at 96/106). R5's D8 range and per-report figures match the reports byte for byte.

findings.claim: The new case never routes a transport-failed row through `summarize`, so the two figures D20 headlines — `infrastructure_failures` and `phases_seen` — are ungraded: a `summarize` that publishes `infrastructure_failures: 0` and `phases_seen: []` regardless of the rows keeps `soak-counts-only-real-completions` green.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:1948-1975 — the submit_failures half calls SK.run_one and asserts only row['phase']; it never calls SK.summarize. The terminal_records half (1977-1996) is the only path into summarize, and every row it builds has a terminal record, i.e. transport_error=None. Its want dict is {completed, correct, attempted, demo_ready} only. Consequence: evals/soak.py:192 (infrastructure_failures) and :203 (phases_seen) — the fields behind D20's '10/10 completed with zero infrastructure failures — no transport error in any phase' (docs/support-matrix.md:65) — have no assertion behind them. Same shape as R1: a green number nothing recomputes; R1's own evidence named infrastructure_failures as one of the three fields at fault.
findings.repro: Patch SK.summarize to force {'infrastructure_failures':0,'phases_seen':[],'not_a_measurement':[]} and run the case -> passed=True (mutation survives). Control: forcing demo_ready=True -> passed=False, so that direction IS pinned.
findings.acceptance: The case feeds at least one row that ended in a transport failure (e.g. the URLError/HTTPError submit rows it already builds) into summarize and asserts infrastructure_failures and phases_seen; hardcoding either to a clean value turns the case red, watched.

findings.claim: ADR-011 Decision 8 claims the case 'pins ... the retry ledger', but the ledger field itself is not pinned — the assertion is a substring search over the whole report, which the per-row `retries` list already satisfies, so `summarize` can drop `transport_retries` entirely and stay green.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:2007 `elif "URLError" not in json.dumps(report)` — report['results'] carries each row's retries list (evals/soak.py:125), so the string is present regardless of evals/soak.py:198-200. R3's acceptance (retried attempts recorded per row with count + phase) is met at the row level — count and phase live only in transport_retries, which is unasserted. ADR-011:307-308 states the stronger claim.
findings.repro: Patch SK.summarize to return {**orig(...), 'transport_retries': []} -> passed=True. Control: dropping the retries= argument at soak.py:129/144 (the real R3 revert) -> passed=False.
findings.acceptance: The retry probe asserts transport_retries content (at least count+phase) so emptying the ledger reddens; or ADR-011 D8 narrows its wording to 'pins that retried attempts are collected per row'.

findings.claim: `_http` appends the final, retry-exhausted attempt to the out-list, so a connect failure that never succeeded is published in `transport_retries` with count 3 and printed under the banner 'connect-phase failures that retried through' — a false label on the exact distinction the ledger was added to make.
findings.evidence: evals/ablation.py:206-212 — retries.append(...) runs on every URLError including the last one before `raise last`; no success/failure marker. evals/soak.py:243-245 prints 'connect-phase failures that retried through: ...' for any row with a non-empty list. Measured on a stubbed hard connect failure: row ends phase=1-client-could-not-connect, infrastructure_failures: 1, AND transport_retries: [{count: 3, ...}] — the same single event reported twice, once with the wrong label.
findings.repro: urlopen stubbed to raise URLError on every POST, AB.RETRY_SLEEPS=(0.0,0.0): transport_retries[0]['count'] == 3 while transport_error is set.
findings.acceptance: Either only attempts followed by a success are recorded, or the entry carries retried_through: bool and the banner reflects it; a case pins that a fully-failed connect produces transport_retries: [] (or retried_through: false).

findings.claim: D8's headline is already stale against artifacts committed in the same PR — it publishes '79.0-79.8s at M9' with six more cases at 93, while the three fast reports this branch commits at the current 95-case suite measure 78.34-79.10s; and its '3.45s of its own run_seconds in each of the four' is 3.46s in two of the four.
findings.evidence: docs/support-matrix.md:78. Branch reports at 95 cases: 20260821-165321-fast.json 79.10, -165559 79.00, -165953 78.34 (below the published minimum). readyz-tracks-the-run-slot got.run_seconds is 3.46 in two of the four cited reports, 3.45 in the others. docs-numbers-are-derived cannot see this: its input.d8.reports list is frozen to the four 93-case reports. This is the class R5 named, one commit later.
findings.repro: Print wall_seconds and result counts from the branch's 95-case fast reports -> [(78.34, 95), (79.0, 95), (79.1, 95)].
findings.acceptance: D8 either cites the newest reports at the current case count or states its range explicitly as 'at 93 cases'; the 3.45s figure is given as a range. Ideally the case derives the cited-report set from the newest N fast reports so it reddens on the next drift.

findings.claim: The new `RETRY_SLEEPS` constant was inserted directly beneath the comment block that documents the 120s socket timeout, so that comment now reads as documenting the backoff tuple it does not describe.
findings.evidence: evals/ablation.py:153-162 — the '30s was too tight ... raised to ~4x the worst observed stall' block describes timeout: int = 120, and RETRY_SLEEPS = (5, 10) is now the first statement after it.
findings.acceptance: The backoff constant sits above its own one-line comment, or the existing block explicitly names the 120s timeout it describes.
